evidence: NUMERICAL ADEQUACY UNRESOLVED: the inherited fractional-weight collision algorithm mixes real weights with integer splitting and an absolute fragment threshold. Its heavy-case replay exhibits large all-or-none collision batches already at decimetre growth and a physically impossible extreme tail. These are exploratory numerical populations, not quantitative snowfall predictions. Removing extreme bins does not validate the smaller population. The audit does not quantify the bias in every case or rule out physical decimetre aggregates. Conditional one-dimensional populations in a persistent liquid-saturated cloud. The condensation supply is imposed; the same collision/fragmentation laws as the earlier study remain. Geometry corrections, seed spread and a resolution control are separate numerical evidence. No resolved turbulence or large-aggregate mechanical fracture is introduced into these populations.
reading_rule: Read the attached numerical_assessment and its hash-identified audit before using sizes or deriving storm optics. The assessment changes evidence metadata only; all original numerical results remain intact. Each run retains number/mass/area moments in logarithmic maximum-dimension bins. freezing_level is a crossing population converted to concentration by individual fall speeds; layers are post-fill time-sampled concentrations in finite layers. projected_area_m2 is per particle, weighted by number concentration; multiply by number_m3 for area density. mass_kg_m3 is already a concentration. summary size percentiles are weighted by arriving mass, not number; the hourly extreme is a cumulative arrival-rate threshold, not a hard maximum. large_tail records raw rare outliers; the final size bin is open above 10 m (null upper edge) and retains its full moments. The export grid is not a physically admitted size range. No local snowfall frequency or habit proportions are inferred. crystals_per_litre normalizes the injected number flux using the fall speed of a 0.2 mm crystal; the injected 0.1–0.4 mm spectrum is not a prescribed size-resolved concentration boundary.
